issue: Defective product replacement and full refund rights
section_title: Right to Replacement or Refund for Defective Goods
legal_text: Where any goods sold to a consumer suffer from a manufacturing defect or fail to perform as specified in the product description, the seller or manufacturer shall be liable to replace the defective item without extra charge or issue a full monetary refund within fourteen calendar days of complaint submission.
plain_explanation: If you buy a product that is defective or doesn't work as advertised, the seller must replace it for free or give you a full refund within 14 days.
applicability: Applies to all retail and e-commerce purchases of physical goods.

issue: Misleading advertising and deceptive price claims
section_title: Prohibition of Unfair Trade Practices and Misleading Ads
legal_text: Any service provider or retailer publishing advertisements containing false representations regarding price, origin, quality, or features of products commits an unfair trade practice. Affected consumers are entitled to compensation and statutory damages up to twice the purchase price.
plain_explanation: Sellers cannot use false advertisements or fake discounts. If they trick you with false claims, you can demand compensation.
applicability: Applies to advertisements, promotional offers, and marketing across print, digital, and broadcast media.

issue: Deficiency of service in e-commerce logistics and non-delivery
section_title: Duties of Digital Platforms regarding Delivery Timelines
legal_text: E-commerce platforms that fail to deliver ordered goods within the confirmed delivery timeline without valid force majeure reasons shall automatically refund the full transaction amount along with a default compensation penalty of 5 percent per week of delay.
plain_explanation: Online stores must deliver your order on time. If they fail without a valid reason, you get a full refund plus a delay penalty.
applicability: Applies to online shopping platforms and third-party sellers.

issue: Warranty void claims based on unauthorized third-party repairs
section_title: Right to Repair and Warranty Protections
legal_text: Manufacturers shall not void a consumer product warranty solely because the consumer engaged an independent technician for routine maintenance, provided the maintenance did not directly cause the alleged defect.
plain_explanation: Companies cannot cancel your warranty just because an independent repair shop did basic maintenance on your device.
applicability: Applies to electronic items, appliances, and motor vehicles.

issue: Hidden charges and un-consented subscription billing
section_title: Mandatory Prior Opt-in for Recurring Commercial Fees
legal_text: No service provider shall levy recurring charges, hidden fees, or automatic subscription renewals without explicit prior affirmative opt-in consent from the account holder.
plain_explanation: Companies cannot add hidden fees or auto-renew subscriptions without your clear prior permission.
applicability: Applies to telecom, software subscriptions, banking, and streaming services.

issue: Adulterated or substandard food items purchased at retail
act: Dummy Food Safety and Standards Regulation, 2024
section_title: Liability for Sale of Contaminated or Expired Foodstuffs
legal_text: Any vendor selling packaged food items beyond their specified expiry date or containing unapproved chemical contaminants shall refund the consumer and reimburse medical expenses incurred as a direct consequence.
plain_explanation: If a shop sells expired or contaminated food that makes you sick, they must refund you and pay your medical expenses.
applicability: Applies to supermarkets, restaurants, and food delivery services.

issue: Unpaid salary and illegal withholding of earned wages
act: Dummy Fair Employment and Wages Act, 2024
legal_text: Employers must disburse accrued wages to employees no later than the 7th working day of the following calendar month. Unreasonable delay beyond 15 days incurs a statutory penalty interest rate of 12 percent per annum payable directly to the employee.
plain_explanation: Your boss must pay your monthly salary by the 7th of every month. If delayed past 15 days, they owe you extra interest.
applicability: Applies to all salaried, contract, and casual workers in commercial establishments.

issue: Overtime work performed without double-rate compensation
act: Dummy Fair Employment and Wages Act, 2024
section_title: Maximum Working Hours and Overtime Pay
legal_text: Working hours exceeding 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week constitute overtime work. Overtime hours must be compensated at not less than twice the worker's ordinary hourly rate.
plain_explanation: If you work more than 8 hours a day or 48 hours a week, your employer must pay you double your hourly rate for extra hours.
applicability: Applies to industrial workers, retail employees, and office staff.

issue: Unsafe working conditions and lack of mandatory safety equipment
act: Dummy Workplace Health and Safety Act, 2024
section_title: Employer Obligations to Provide Safety Apparel and Hazards Mitigation
legal_text: Employers are strictly mandated to supply protective gear, safety equipment, and clean drinking water to all personnel exposed to physical or environmental hazards without deducting expenses from employee wages.
plain_explanation: Employers must provide free safety gear and clean water. They cannot charge you or deduct money for required safety equipment.
applicability: Applies to construction sites, factories, warehouses, and sanitation work.

issue: Denial of paid maternity leave and benefit entitlement
section_title: Entitlement to Paid Maternity Leave and Job Protection
legal_text: Every woman employed for at least 80 days in the preceding twelve months is entitled to 26 weeks of fully paid maternity leave. It is illegal to terminate an employee during or on account of maternity leave.
plain_explanation: Female workers who completed 80 days of work are entitled to 26 weeks of fully paid maternity leave. Employers cannot fire a pregnant employee.
applicability: Applies to all private and public establishments employing 10 or more persons.

issue: Abrupt termination of employment without contractual notice or severance
act: Dummy Fair Employment and Wages Act, 2024
section_title: Mandatory Notice Period and Severance Compensation
legal_text: No employer shall terminate a permanent worker without serving 30 days written notice or providing salary in lieu of notice, alongside severance pay calculated as 15 days salary per completed year of service.
plain_explanation: Bosses cannot fire regular employees without 30 days notice or 30 days pay, plus 15 days of salary for every year worked.
applicability: Applies to permanent employees with at least one year of continuous service.

issue: Gender-based wage discrimination for identical work roles
section_title: Equal Remuneration for Men and Women Workers
legal_text: Employers shall pay equal wages to male and female employees performing the same work or work of a similar nature under similar working conditions without discrimination based on gender.
plain_explanation: Men and women doing the same job must receive equal pay.
applicability: Applies to all employers and employment agencies.

issue: Unlawful retention of rental security deposit by landlord
section_title: Limits on Security Deposit and Refund Deadlines
legal_text: The security deposit for residential premises shall not exceed two months rent. Landlords must refund the full security deposit, minus itemized actual damages, within thirty days of tenant vacation of premises.
plain_explanation: Your security deposit cannot be more than 2 months rent. The landlord must return it within 30 days of moving out, deducting only proven repair costs.

issue: Unilateral and arbitrary increase in monthly rent during lease period
section_title: Rent Revision Rules and Notice Requirements
legal_text: Landlords cannot increase rent during an active lease agreement unless agreed upon in writing. Annual rent escalation shall not exceed 7 percent and requires three months prior written notice.
plain_explanation: Landlords cannot raise rent in the middle of a fixed lease. Yearly rent increases cannot exceed 7% and need 3 months written notice.
applicability: Applies to all registered residential lease agreements.

issue: Landlord refusing essential structural repairs and maintenance
legal_text: Landlords are responsible for structural repairs, roof leaks, and electrical safety. If the landlord fails to carry out essential repairs within 15 days of notice, the tenant may perform repairs and deduct cost from monthly rent.
plain_explanation: Landlords must fix major structural or roof issues. If they ignore your 15-day notice, you can fix it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent.

issue: Forced eviction without proper notice or court order
legal_text: No landlord shall evict a tenant or enter rented premises forcibly without serving a valid 30-day notice specifying statutory grounds and securing an eviction order from the competent Rent Authority.
plain_explanation: A landlord cannot lock you out or force you to leave without giving a 30-day written notice and obtaining an official court order.
applicability: Applies to all residential and commercial tenants.

issue: Cut-off of water or electricity supply by landlord to force tenant exit
section_title: Prohibition of Withholding Essential Utility Services
legal_text: No landlord or property agent shall disconnect essential services including water, electricity, sanitary connections, or elevator access to force tenant compliance or eviction. Breach incurs immediate Restoration Orders and fines.
plain_explanation: Landlords are legally forbidden from cutting off your water, electricity, or gas to force you to leave or pay disputed fees.

issue: Unannounced landlord intrusions violating tenant privacy
section_title: Tenant Right to Privacy and Landlord Entry Protocol
legal_text: Landlords must provide at least 24 hours prior written notice before entering leased premises for inspections or repairs. Entry must take place during reasonable daytime hours (8:00 AM to 6:00 PM).
plain_explanation: Landlords must give you at least 24 hours written notice before coming over for inspection, and visits must happen during daytime hours.
